## Create a client

```go
import streams "example.com/streams"

client, err := streams.NewStreamsClient(streams.Config{
	Endpoint: os.Getenv("STREAMS_ENDPOINT"),
	Token:    func(context.Context) (string, error) { return os.Getenv("STREAMS_TOKEN"), nil },

if err != nil {

}
```

		Endpoint: os.Getenv("STREAMS_ENDPOINT"),
		Token:    func(context.Context) (string, error) { return os.Getenv("STREAMS_TOKEN"), nil },

## Errors

Each modelled error is a struct such as `*streams.ValidationError`, matched with `errors.As(err, &target)`; its `Metadata` (`*streams.ServiceError`) carries the HTTP status, request ID and headers. Every service error satisfies `streams.StreamsException`; an unmodelled one is a `*streams.ServiceError`, a transport failure a `*streams.NetworkError`, and cancellation and deadlines keep their context errors. Streaming calls return *ResponseStream[Item]. Always defer Close; Next, Value and Err consume it on demand. The caller context and total timeout remain active through body consumption, including idle time before the first read. Closing releases only that response. Successful headers are never replayed. Config.MaxStreamEventBytes bounds frames and opening error bodies (default 1 MiB, minimum 256). Invalid profiles report *StreamProtocolError.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. For operations that declare an idempotency token, an unset token is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. Set `Config.MaxAttempts` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off) and `Config.RetryMode` to `streams.RetryModeStandard` or `streams.RetryModeAdaptive` for a shared retry quota or client-side rate limiting.
